title: The research, validation and delegation adapters call the implementations that already exist
statement: Each registered research and validation tool performs its work by calling the existing implementation in `lib/` rather than restating its rules: no capability decision, retrieval policy or validation rule is re-implemented in the wrapper. A capability call reports what is available and changes nothing - no planning content, no configuration and no stored state. Every result and every refusal is structured data, and neither carries a credential, a credential-derived value or an absolute user path.
notes: ⚠️ SPLIT FROM ACC-0065, WHICH ACCEPTED TWO TASKS THAT DO NOT DEPEND ON EACH OTHER. That criterion is about the write discipline of mutation wrappers - TSK-0044's work - and would have held TSK-0045 behind it while describing almost none of what TSK-0045 builds. ⚠️ A CAPABILITY CALL IS A READ, AND "CHANGES NOTHING" MEANS NO PERSISTED CHANGE. It mutates no planning content, no configuration and no stored state - no credential cached, no choice recorded, no file written. It does NOT mean the call touches nothing: `research_capability` makes a live request to the backend and `validation_capability` runs the interpreter, because #121 requires a capability to be PROVEN rather than declared, and #67 measured what a declared-but-unusable capability costs. A test asserting no request and no subprocess would contradict the rule the probes exist to satisfy; what must be asserted is that nothing persisted changed. ⚠️ DELEGATION IS NO LONGER HERE (F80, 2026-09-12). This criterion required each registered delegation tool to call "the existing implementation in `lib/`", and no delegation runtime exists there: it is CMP-0036's, built by TSK-0053 and TSK-0054, which TSK-0045 does not depend on. As written the criterion could not be satisfied by the task it accepts. `kiln_delegate` is now registered by TSK-0053 beside the runtime it builds, under its own criterion. ⚠️ THE FIVE WIRE NAMES ARE UNPREFIXED, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE (F79). `research_capability`, `research_search`, `research_fetch`, `validation_capability` and `validation_run` are the names `lib/specialists/contract.mjs` requires by key and `verifyChild` checks a child against; renaming them to `kiln_*` would break the contract and the child-signature check. ⚠️ THE SIGNATURE TOOL IS ACC-0109's, NOT THIS ONE'S. `kiln_capability` returning the package's declaration unchanged is accepted there; this covers the adapters beside it. ⚠️ THE PI WRAPPER IS THE DISCLOSURE BOUNDARY; THE VALIDATION CONTROLLER IS DELIBERATELY NOT (F84, 2026-09-12). Measured against the real lib/validation/: a validation_run result carries absolute machine paths by four routes - failure.message when provisioning fails (the interpreter and the vpw-tier1- workspace), destroy.retainedPath and the retained-workspace omission reason when cleanup leaves the workspace behind, and executions[].stderr or stdout when a job prints its own paths, as a Python traceback does. The controller keeps those precise paths on purpose, as diagnostics for its own callers, and is not changed. The Pi wrapper renders a sanitised COPY - the exact workspace root becomes <workspace> with its relative tail kept, the interpreter, temporary directory and home become <path>, and a general absolute-path scrub runs last - and leaves the controller object untouched. A separate controller issue is warranted only if another model-facing or persisted consumer shows a controller result without going through this boundary. ⚠️ CREDENTIAL BOUNDARY (D5). Import and registration read no environment. At handler invocation, the wrapper delegates without collecting credentials for redaction; the invoked research and validation implementations may read their own permitted environment inputs. The validation controller constructs the allowlisted child environment, and tests prove a planted credential reaches neither the controller result nor the rendered result.
